# Epidural Steroid Injection Clinical Compass

## CPT Codes

| CPT | Description | RVU | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 62321 | Injection(s), of diagnostic or therapeutic substance(s) (eg, anesthetic, antispasmodic, opioid, steroid, other solution), not including neurolytic substances; cervical or thoracic, interlaminar epidural | 3.82 | Cervical/thoracic interlaminar ESI |
| 62323 | Injection(s), of diagnostic or therapeutic substance(s); lumbar or sacral, interlaminar epidural | 3.62 | Lumbar/sacral interlaminar ESI |
| 64479 | Injection(s), anesthetic agent and/or steroid, transforaminal epidural; cervical or thoracic, single level | 4.12 | Cervical/thoracic TFESI — single level |
| 64480 | Injection(s), anesthetic agent and/or steroid, transforaminal epidural; cervical or thoracic, each additional level | 2.18 | Additional level — add-on code |
| 64483 | Injection(s), anesthetic agent and/or steroid, transforaminal epidural; lumbar or sacral, single level | 3.92 | Lumbar/sacral TFESI — single level |
| 64484 | Injection(s), anesthetic agent and/or steroid, transforaminal epidural; lumbar or sacral, each additional level | 2.08 | Additional level — add-on code |
| 62311 | Injection(s), of diagnostic or therapeutic substance(s); lumbar or sacral, caudal epidural | 3.44 | Caudal ESI |

## ICD-10 Codes

| ICD-10 | Description | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| M54.4 | Lumbago with sciatica | Lumbar radiculopathy — most common indication |
| M54.42 | Lumbago with sciatica, left side |  |
| M54.41 | Lumbago with sciatica, right side |  |
| M54.12 | Radiculopathy, cervical region | Cervical radiculopathy |
| M54.13 | Radiculopathy, cervicothoracic region |  |
| M48.061 | Spinal stenosis, lumbar region with neurogenic claudication | Lumbar stenosis with claudication |
| M51.16 | Intervertebral disc degeneration, lumbar region | Lumbar DDD |
| M51.17 | Intervertebral disc degeneration, lumbosacral region |  |

## Payer Requirements

Tabs: Medicare | Medicaid | Private Insurance

### Medicare

**Prior Authorization Requirements**
- MRI or CT confirming nerve root compression or stenosis correlating with symptoms
- Documentation of conservative therapy failure: ≥4–6 weeks PT and/or NSAIDs
- Dermatomal distribution of radicular symptoms documented
- Physician attestation of medical necessity
- Frequency limit: typically 3 injections per region per year (Medicare LCD)

**Medical Necessity Criteria**
- ✓ Radicular pain with imaging-confirmed nerve root compression
- ✓ Neurogenic claudication from lumbar spinal stenosis
- ✓ Acute disc herniation with severe radiculopathy
- ✓ Failed conservative therapy (PT, NSAIDs) for ≥4 weeks

**Reimbursement:** Medicare covers ESI under LCD L35090 (or applicable regional LCD). Fluoroscopic guidance (77003) is separately billable. Frequency limits apply — document each injection date and response.

**Known Payer Policies**

| Payer | Policy | Covered |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Medicare (CMS) | Covered per LCD; 3 injections/region/year; fluoroscopy separately billable (77003) | Yes |

### Medicaid

**Prior Authorization Requirements**
- State-specific prior authorization required in most states
- MRI or CT confirming pathology
- Documentation of conservative therapy failure
- Physician attestation

**Medical Necessity Criteria**
- ✓ Radicular pain with imaging correlation
- ✓ Failed conservative therapy

**Reimbursement:** Medicaid coverage and frequency limits vary significantly by state. Many states require prior authorization for ESI. Rates are typically lower than Medicare.

**Known Payer Policies**

| Payer | Policy | Covered |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Medicaid (state-specific) | Prior auth required in most states; frequency limits vary | Yes |

### Private Insurance

**Prior Authorization Requirements**
- Prior authorization required by most commercial payers
- MRI or CT report confirming nerve root compression or stenosis
- Documentation of conservative therapy failure: ≥4–6 weeks PT
- Dermatomal symptom documentation
- Frequency limit: typically 3 injections per region per year
- Peer-to-peer review may be required after 2+ injections

**Medical Necessity Criteria**
- ✓ Radicular pain with imaging-confirmed nerve root compression
- ✓ Neurogenic claudication from stenosis
- ✓ Failed conservative therapy (PT, NSAIDs, oral steroids)

**Reimbursement:** Commercial payers typically cover ESI with prior authorization. Bundling rules for fluoroscopy (77003) vary — verify payer-specific policies. Some payers require step therapy (oral steroids before ESI).

**Known Payer Policies**

| Payer | Policy | Covered |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Aetna | Covered; requires MRI and 4-week PT failure; 3/region/year limit | Yes |
| UnitedHealthcare | Covered with prior auth; MRI and PT documentation required | Yes |
| BCBS (most plans) | Covered; 3 injections/region/year; prior auth required | Yes |
| Cigna | Covered with prior auth; imaging correlation required | Yes |
| Humana | Covered; prior auth and conservative therapy documentation required | Yes |

## Required Documentation

### Imaging
- □ MRI or CT spine with radiologist report confirming disc herniation, stenosis, or nerve root compression
- □ Correlation between imaging level and dermatomal symptoms documented

### Clinical Documentation
- □ H&P documenting radicular symptom distribution (dermatomal pattern)
- □ Pain scores at multiple visits (NRS or VAS)
- □ Functional impairment documentation
- □ Prior injection dates and response (if repeat injection)

### Conservative Therapy
- □ PT notes documenting ≥4–6 weeks of lumbar/cervical stabilization program
- □ NSAIDs or oral steroid trial documentation
- □ Activity modification documentation

### Procedure Documentation
- □ Fluoroscopy confirmation of needle placement (77003)
- □ Contrast injection confirming epidural spread
- □ Steroid agent, dose, and volume documentation

## Submission Process

1. Obtain MRI or CT confirming nerve root compression or stenosis at symptomatic level
2. Document dermatomal distribution of radicular symptoms correlating with imaging
3. Document conservative therapy failure (≥4–6 weeks PT and NSAIDs)
4. Submit prior authorization with CPT codes (62323 or 64483 for lumbar), ICD-10 codes, and clinical documentation
5. Include MRI report, PT notes, and pain scores
6. Document prior injection dates and response for repeat injections
7. If denied, request peer-to-peer review citing imaging correlation and PT failure
8. For frequency limit denials, document medical necessity for additional injection

## Common Denial Reasons

- ⚠ Frequency limit exceeded (3/region/year) — document exceptional circumstances for additional injections
- ⚠ Imaging not confirming nerve root compression at symptomatic level — ensure MRI/CT correlates with dermatomal symptoms
- ⚠ Insufficient conservative therapy documentation (document ≥4–6 weeks PT explicitly)
- ⚠ Missing dermatomal symptom distribution documentation
- ⚠ Fluoroscopy (77003) not separately authorized — verify payer bundling rules
- ⚠ Wrong CPT code for approach (interlaminar vs. transforaminal vs. caudal)
- ⚠ Prior authorization not obtained before procedure
